To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
RsmA directly activates phz2 expression by destabilizing the stem-loop structure in the phzA2 5′-UTR, while it represses phz1 expression through the binding of the SD sequence.

(1) the third GGA (S3) motif of the 5′UTR of the phzA2 transcript, but not the GGA motifs of the phz1 transcript, is directly bound by RsmA and is involved in direct activation of phzA2 transcription; and (2) RsmA-mediated repression of phz1 expression may be a result of the binding of RSmA near the SD sequence, which blocks ribosome access.
RsmA-mediated regulation of the phz clusters in M18 is differentially exerted at the translational level, and that the phzA2 promoter is directly regulated by RsmA.

the identification of novel RsmA-mediated mechanisms that control gene expression in P. aerugenosa M18.

the RsmA family of RNA-binding proteins in P. aerugionsa M18 regulates the expression of both the phz1 and phz2 gene clusters at the post-translational level.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
RsmA is a versatile post-transcriptional regulator in P. aeriginosa, which is involved in the regulation of both positive and negative feedback control of the phenazine biosyntheses.
RsmA is a versatile regulator that can either repress or activate translation initiation at target genes.
